title: The Fourier-analytic weight of a pure real sheaf equals its weight
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a nonzero lisse
$\iota$-real Weil sheaf, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Then

$$
\|\mathcal G\|=w
$$

in the $L^2$-weight parameter of [def-wf-l2-norm].

proof.text: Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal G$, with the tensor descent automorphism. The tensor equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations], clause (2), shows that the underlying tensor is lisse and that its stalk is the tensor of the stalks. Here $X$ is connected, Noetherian and separated, and $\ell$ is invertible, as required by that clause. The tensor action on a stalk is the diagonal action of [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. By [p-linear-spectra], its local eigenvalues at a closed point $x$ are all $\alpha_i\alpha_j$, with multiplicity, where the $\alpha_i$ are those of $\mathcal G$. By [def-weil-punctual-weights] each product has realized absolute value $q_x^w$, so $\mathcal T$ is punctually pure of weight $2w$.

source.place: Paragraphs 1 and 3: tensor construction and punctual weight.

proof.text: Reality in [def-wf-iota-real] says that the realized local eigenvalue multiset of $\mathcal G$ is its own complex conjugate. Thus $\mathcal G$ itself may serve as the second sheaf with conjugate local spectra in [lem-wf-conjugate-tensor-traces]; no conjugate coefficient-field functor is needed. Apply that lemma to obtain, for the Euler series $L(t)=L(X_0,\mathcal T,t)$, the formal identity $\varphi_{\mathcal G}L=L'$, where $\varphi_{\mathcal G}(t)=\sum_{m\geq1}S_m t^{m-1}$ and $S_m=\|f_{\mathcal G}\|_m^2$ are the nonnegative real trace energies of [def-wf-l2-series]. Since $L(0)=1$, this is $\varphi_{\mathcal G}=L'/L$ in $\mathbf C[[t]]$.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2: logarithmic derivative of the Euler series.

proof.text: Apply [cor-rp-euler-product] to the lisse sheaf $\mathcal T$ on $X_0$ and transport its polynomial coefficients by $\iota$. It gives $L=A_0/B_0$, where $A_0(t)=\iota\det(1-tF\mid H_c^1(X,\mathcal T))$ and $B_0(t)=\iota\det(1-tF\mid H_c^2(X,\mathcal T))$, both with constant term one. Thus $L$ is rational. The cited corollary already states the two-term cohomological formula, so no additional vanishing assertion is being inferred from a definition.

Apply [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints] with $U_0=C_0=X_0$, $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal T$. This verifies its dense-open and lissity hypotheses and gives purity of $H_c^2(X,\mathcal T)$ of weight $2w+2$. By [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], each eigenvalue $\alpha$ of its Frobenius has $|\iota\alpha|=q^{w+1}$. Hence every root of $B_0$ has absolute value $R=q^{-w-1}>0$. This assertion permits $H_c^2=0$ and $B_0=1$ at this stage; existence of a surviving denominator root will be proved below.

source.place: Paragraph 3: all possible denominator roots lie on one circle.

proof.text: The nonempty affine scheme $X_0$ is quasi-compact and Kolmogorov; [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] supplies a closed point $x$. Its degree $d\geq1$ is finite by [def-weil-closed-point-degree]. Choose a geometric point above $x$. Clause (2) of [cor-galois-lisse-representations], now using that point as base point of the connected scheme $X$, makes the stalk functor an equivalence. A zero stalk would therefore make the underlying sheaf zero, and then its Weil object zero, contrary to the hypothesis. Write $r=\dim\mathcal G_{\bar x}>0$. The tensor stalk has dimension $r^2$ and invertible Frobenius. Its local denominator $P_x(t)=\iota\det(1-F_xt^d\mid\mathcal T_{\bar x})$ consequently has degree $dr^2>0$, nonzero leading coefficient and constant term one. Its inverse series cannot be a polynomial: otherwise the polynomial product $P_xP_x^{-1}=1$ would have positive degree.

source.place: Paragraph 4: a closed point with a nonzero stalk and a nonpolynomial local factor.

proof.text: By [lem-rp-even-tensor-positivity], clause (ii) with tensor exponent $2$, every local inverse characteristic polynomial of $\mathcal T$ has nonnegative real coefficients and constant term one. Substitution $t\mapsto t^{d(y)}$ preserves both properties. For a fixed degree $n$, the Euler product of step 3 involves only finitely many factors contributing a nonconstant term in degrees at most $n$. In its coefficient of degree $n$, choosing the term from the factor at $x$ and constant terms from all other factors shows $[t^n]L\geq[t^n]P_x^{-1}\geq0$. The local inverse of step 5 has infinitely many nonzero coefficients, so $L$ does too. In particular $L$ is not a polynomial. Cancel common factors in $A_0/B_0$ to write $L=A/B$ with $A,B$ coprime. Then $B$ is nonconstant, has a complex root $a$, and $A(a)\ne0$. Because $B$ divides $B_0$, step 4 gives $|a|=R$; also $A(0)B(0)\ne0$.

Let $m\geq1$ be the multiplicity of $a$ as a root of $B$, and write $B=(t-a)^m b$ with $b(a)
e0$. Logarithmic differentiation of the rational identity $L=A/B$ gives
$$\varphi_{\mathcal G}= rac{A'}A- rac m{t-a}- rac{b'}b= rac{C}{D},\qquad C=(t-a)(A'b-Ab')-mAb,\quad D=(t-a)Ab.$$
Here $D(0)
e0$ since $a
e0$, $A(0)
e0$ and $B(0)
e0$. Moreover $D(a)=0$ and $C(a)=-mA(a)b(a)
e0$, since the coefficients have characteristic zero. The identity is also the formal identity $D\varphi_{\mathcal G}=C$ at zero, by [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Apply [lem-wf-rational-series-pole-radius] to these explicitly given polynomials to obtain $r_{\mathcal G}\leq |a|=R$. This calculation requires no weight bound on $H_c^1$.

source.place: Final paragraph: an explicit uncancelled denominator for the logarithmic derivative, then its radius bound.

proof.text: Punctual purity of weight $w$ implies mixedness of weights at most $w$ by the one-step filtration $0\subset\mathcal G$ in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Hence [lem-wf-l2-upper] gives $\|\mathcal G\|\leq w$. By [lem-wf-l2-radius], $r_{\mathcal G}=q^{-\|\mathcal G\|-1}\geq q^{-w-1}=R$ since $q>1$. Together with step 7 this gives $r_{\mathcal G}=R$, a finite positive radius. The same radius identity, or its logarithmic form, now yields $\|\mathcal G\|=-1-\log_q(R)=w$.

source.place: Final paragraph: the upper weight estimate and radius identity give equality.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof; polynomial identity spelling out the final pole calculation.
